components.title: Part A: tiered pricing, discount, and tax
components.what: Compute the 757-unit subtotal using 100 units at 6.40, 200 units at 5.44, and the remaining units at 4.48; apply the 8% discount to the entire subtotal because it exceeds 2500, then apply 7.25% sales tax, retaining precision until rounding the final total to cents.

components.title: Part B: monthly account simulation
components.what: Starting from 1200, apply each month’s listed transaction first, charge a 12 fee whenever the resulting balance is below 1000, then add interest equal to 0.4% of that post-fee balance; simulate all 15 months and round only the final balance to cents.

components.title: Part C: investment growth simulation
components.what: For each of 12 periods, add the listed contribution, multiply the balance by 1.025, then deduct 0.75% of the grown balance; retain full precision through all periods and round only the final balance to cents.

components.title: Part D: amortization with extra principal
components.what: Compute the standard monthly payment for a 12000 loan at a monthly rate of 0.078/12 over 60 months, then simulate 18 payments; in months 3 and 16, apply the additional 300 and 1000 principal with that month’s regular payment, retaining full precision until rounding the remaining balance after month

The draft applies the 8% discount and 7.25% tax in one multiplication: 3775.36 × 0.92 × 1.0725 = 3725.147712. But 0.92 × 1.0725 = 0.9867, and 3775.36 × 0.9867 = 3725.147712, which rounds to $3725.15. However, the subtotal after discount is 3775.36 × 0.92 = 3473.3312, which is not a whole-cent amount. If the discount is applied first and rounded to the nearest cent before tax, the discounted subtotal is $3473.33, and tax is 3473.33 × 0.0725 = 251.816425, giving a total of 3725.146425, which rounds to $3725.15. So the answer is the same, but the working conflates rounding. The claim is numerically correct but the working is ambiguous about rounding order.

The draft subtracts the $12 fee in month 13 because the balance after the withdrawal is 1395.845 - 900 = 495.845, which is below $1,000. That is correct. The calculation is correct.
The draft's month 13 value is 485.773, but the correct value is 485.7805 (see previous challenge). This error propagates through months 14 and 15, changing the final balance.

The draft multiplies growth and fee factors together and applies them as a single factor each period. This is correct because the fee is 0.75% of the balance after growth, so the balance after fee is balance × 1.025 × (1 - 0.0075) = balance × 1.025 × 0.9925 = balance × 1.0173125.
